findings.title: Review part failure now returns a result instead of raising, with a misleading log
findings.description:
In the `except ProviderError` branch of the part-running method, the old `raise` is replaced by `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error ...")` and `return self._exception_result(...)`. Two problems follow.
- A named provider failure is logged as "unexpected" with a full traceback. The dispatch action deliberately avoids tracebacks for these (issue 200).
- The method now returns an `ActionResult` where it used to propagate. I did not verify that the callers (`_gated_parts` and the split-review path) handle a failed result from one part the same way they handled the exception. This is the likeliest regression, because a split review could keep going or aggregate wrongly after a part fails. No test in the diff covers a failed part in a split review.

findings.title: Effort lookup in the failure handler can mask the original error
findings.description: `effort_sent_by_profile(...)` calls `get_profile`, `ensure_provider_loaded` and `get_provider`. It runs inside the `except ProviderError` handler, so if any of those raises, the original provider error is lost. Compute the effort before the `try`, or reuse the value that the call path already determined.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews --json` prints plain text when the review directory is missing
findings.description: `stats_reviews` checks `report.missing_dir` before `as_json`. It echoes "No review directory at ..." and exits 0. A script piping `--json` into a parser gets invalid JSON. Emit the empty JSON report (the dataclass already carries `missing_dir`), or exit non-zero.

findings.title: The "warn once per alias" pricing guarantee does not hold on the review path
findings.description: `run_review_with_profile` calls `resolve_cost(alias, ..., set())` with a fresh set on every call, and does so again on the failure path. The executor's `UsageCapture(set())` documents one warning per alias per run. Every review would warn again, so a run with several reviews logs the same pricing warning repeatedly. Passing a shared warning set in would fix this. The bare `set()` argument also exposes an awkward `UsageCapture(set())` constructor that all tests must repeat.

findings.title: Rendering depends on the live alias table
findings.description: The "api-rate equiv." label is decided at report time from the current alias config. Renaming an alias or changing its `cost_tier` relabels old runs. Persisting the tier in the `UsageRecord` would make historical reports stable.

findings.title: Exception used as control flow in the usage row parser
findings.description: The code raises `ValueError` inside the `try` only so its own `except` catches it. A plain `isinstance` check that returns the unreadable row would be clearer.

findings.title: Slice filter on a missing frontmatter key
findings.description: `str(front.get("slice")) == slice_filter` turns a missing key into the string `"None"`. A user filtering by the literal `None` would match every artifact with no slice. Use an explicit `None` check.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of a missing usage capture
findings.description: `require_capture` raises `UsageCaptureMissingError` outside any `try` in the compact and summary actions. In dispatch it is caught by the catch-all and returned as a failed result. The behavior is tested, but the contract differs by action.

findings.title: Usage reading and telemetry design
findings.description: The usage reader parses defensively: bools are rejected, malformed fields become `None` with a warning, and per-message usage is ignored. Telemetry is summed over every result and carried on errors. Token and cost totals keep `None` instead of 0. Tests cover the real captured fixture, partial results, stalls, and state round-tripping.
